questions.question_text: Which one of the following is a vector quantity?

options.why: Mass is a size only; it has no direction, so it is a scalar.
Time is a size only; it has no direction, so it is a scalar.
Area is a size only; it has no direction, so it is a scalar.

questions.solution_text:
A vector needs a size and a direction.
Only the force states a direction, downwards, as well as a size of $40$ N.
The downward force of $40$ N is the vector.

questions.question_text:
How many of these four quantities are vectors?
a speed of $25$ m/s, a velocity of $25$ m/s upwards, a temperature of $19^{\circ}\text{C}$, a displacement of $6$ m south

options.why: Counted only the displacement and missed that a velocity also states a direction.
Counted the speed as a vector; a speed gives a size only, with no direction.
Counted every quantity that has a number and a unit, rather than checking for a direction.

questions.solution_text:
A speed of $25$ m/s gives a size only, so it is a scalar.
A temperature of $19^{\circ}\text{C}$ gives a size only, so it is a scalar.
The velocity upwards and the displacement south each give a size and a direction.
$2$ of the quantities are vectors.

options.why: Reversing the vector reverses its direction, not the sign of its magnitude; a length is never negative.
Added the two lengths as if the trip out and back were one vector.
Confused the reversed vector with the sum of a vector and its negative.

questions.question_text:
$\underset{\sim}{u}$ is the velocity of a yacht.
What does $|\underset{\sim}{u}|$ describe?

options.text: The direction the yacht is heading
options.why: The bars keep the size and discard the direction, not the other way round.

options.text: The distance the yacht has travelled
options.why: Read the bars as a total journey length; they give the magnitude of the velocity itself.
A velocity describes how fast and which way, so its magnitude cannot be a position.

questions.solution_text:
$|\underset{\sim}{u}|$ is the magnitude of the velocity vector $\underset{\sim}{u}$.
The magnitude of a velocity is how fast the yacht is going, with the direction removed.
$|\underset{\sim}{u}|$ is the speed of the yacht.

questions.question_text: Which of these expressions is meaningful?

options.why: Adds the scalar $3$ to a vector; a number with no direction cannot be added to a directed quantity.
Subtracts a vector from the scalar $8$, which mixes a directed quantity with a plain number.
$|\underset{\sim}{a}|$ is a magnitude, which is a scalar, so it cannot be added to the vector $\underset{\sim}{b}$.

questions.solution_text:
A scalar may multiply a vector, and a vector may be added to or subtracted from another vector.
In $4\underset{\sim}{a}-\underset{\sim}{b}$ the scalar $4$ multiplies $\underset{\sim}{a}$, and the vector $\underset{\sim}{b}$ is subtracted from the vector $4\underset{\sim}{a}$.
$4\underset{\sim}{a}-\underset{\sim}{b}$ is the meaningful expression.

options.why: Read the letters in alphabetical order instead of from the tail to the arrowhead.
The bars name the length of the segment, which is a scalar, not the vector itself.
Reverses the letters and adds bars, naming a length rather than the vector drawn.

questions.solution_text:

questions.question_text:
Three of the quantities below are vectors.
Which one is the odd one out?

options.why: A velocity states a size and a direction, so it is a vector like the other two.

options.text: A force of $12$ N to the left
options.why: A force acts in a stated direction, so it is a vector like the other two.
Weight is the pull of gravity acting downwards, so it is a force and therefore a vector.

questions.solution_text:
A journey length is a total distance travelled, and a distance has no direction attached to it.
The other three each state a direction as well as a size.
The journey length of $15$ km is the odd one out, because it is a scalar.

questions.question_text: Which pair contains one vector and one scalar?

options.why: Both state a direction as well as a size, so both are vectors.
Both are sizes only, so both are scalars.
Both are sizes only, so both are scalars.

questions.solution_text:
Speed gives how fast only, with no direction, so it is a scalar.
Displacement gives how far and in which direction, so it is a vector.
Speed and displacement is the pair with one of each.
